papers.title: Bilevel Coordinated Reflection: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.desc: Multi-agent LLM systems commonly use an orchestrator to decompose a task for a team of workers and then improve through textual reflection.

papers.title: The Attention Triangle in Audio-Video Models
papers.desc: Audio-video diffusion models rely on cross-modal attention to coordinate text, sound, and visual content, yet this same mechanism can introduce subtle and systematic semantic leakage.

papers.title: Enoki: Efficient Multi-Level Hallucination Detection
papers.desc: Ensuring factuality remains a critical challenge for deploying LLMs in high-stakes settings.

papers.title: Beneath the Surface of Chains-of-Thought: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Reasoning Operations in LLMs
papers.desc: Reasoning in large language models unfolds through diverse functional operations, such as problem formulation, goal decomposition, and deduction.

papers.title: UniMate: One Unified Model to Animate Diverse Skeletons
papers.desc: Recent advances in automatic rigging now deliver animation-ready 3D assets at scale, yet generating the motion to drive them remains a bottleneck.

papers.title: One Editor, Many Edits: A Unified Training-Free Framework for Diverse Video Editing
papers.desc: Video editing spans diverse editing paradigms, yet achieving high-quality instruction-guided and subject-guided editing within a single unified framework remains challenging.

papers.title: Dr. Claw: An AI Scientist Workspace for Vibe Research
papers.desc: Command-line coding agents (e.g., Claude Code, Gemini CLI) can already read and write files and sustain long sessions, yet end-to-end research still fragments across chat tools, IDEs, terminals, and writing environments, and the decisions that make it auditable are rarely preserved.

papers.title: Training-Free Speech-Centric Omni Understanding with Frozen VLMs
papers.desc: Audio-visual understanding remains challenging because models must jointly interpret spoken content, visual events, and their temporal relationships.

papers.title: τ^τ-Bench: An Environment for End-To-End, Realistic Agent Construction
papers.desc: LLM agents are rapidly becoming production software, deployed to handle customer service, adjudicate disputes, and operate internal systems.

papers.title: To See a World in a Living Context: Unified Indoor-Outdoor Urban World Generation
papers.desc: Text-driven 3D generation has advanced rapidly in creating large-scale outdoor environments and detailed indoor scenes, but these domains are usually synthesized independently, lacking the correspondence required for a coherent urban world.

papers.title: ShallowStream: Index Shallow then Answer Deep for Streaming Video Understanding
papers.desc: Streaming video understanding is a critical capability for real-world applications, including embodied intelligence, autonomous driving, industrial monitoring, surveillance and early warning, and wearable assistants.

papers.title: Knowing What Not to Answer: Selective Non-Compliance in Vision-Language Models
papers.desc: Vision-language models (VLMs) are expected to respond helpfully to appropriate requests while withholding compliance with requests that are incorrect, unsafe, infeasible, or unanswerable.

papers.title: Refuse without Refusal: A Structural Analysis of Safety-Tuning Responses for Reducing False Refusals in Language Models
papers.desc: Striking a balance between helpfulness and safety remains a fundamental challenge in aligning large language models.

papers.title: The 2026 PNPL Competition: Word Classification and Efficient Cross-Subject Generalisation in LibriBrain100
papers.desc: The ambition of the 2025 PNPL competition (Landau et al., 2025) was to launch a multi-year curriculum for non-invasive speech decoding.

papers.title: HarvestBench: Measuring Whether LLM Agents Will Pay to Avoid Killing Animals
papers.desc: Benchmarks for the side effects an agent causes on the way to a goal already exist, but HarvestBench is the first to put a price on avoiding the side effect and to name that side effect as a living creature.
